rationale: C17 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both letters implement the same February 6 balance-of-payments program through legislation designed to make dollar holdings more attractive to foreign central banks and thereby reduce conversions into U.S. gold. They also share a distinctive administrative sequence: attach draft legislation, explain its role in defending the gold reserve, compare government obligations with time deposits, attach a Treasury memorandum, and ask that the legislation be laid before the House. C15 shares the same policy program and legislative-transmittal form but lacks this close machinery; C22 has a similar Kennedy-era transmittal structure but concerns an unrelated program.

shared_material.child_excerpt: permitting banks in this country to pay different rates of interest on time deposits held here by foreign governments than are paid to domestic depositors
shared_material.parent_excerpt: foreign central banks would be exempt from tax on interest they derive from holding obligations issued by the United States Government
shared_material.explanation: Both propose special financial treatment intended to make dollar-denominated assets more attractive to foreign official holders.

shared_material.child_excerpt: implements a recommendation contained in my message to the Congress dated February 6, 1961, relating to the balance of payments problem
shared_material.parent_excerpt: one of various desirable steps, mentioned in my Message to the Congress of February 6, intended to improve this country's ability to defend its gold reserve
shared_material.explanation: Both identify themselves as components of the same presidential legislative program.

shared_material.child_excerpt: those governments will be encouraged to maintain dollar accounts in this country rather than require the United States to convert their dollar accounts to gold
shared_material.parent_excerpt: offering competitively attractive dollar obligations to foreign central banks... as an alternative to holding gold
shared_material.explanation: The distinctive policy mechanism is the same: use more attractive dollar returns to discourage official conversion into gold.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Also transmitted is a memorandum from the Secretary of the Treasury describing the draft bill and its impact in detail.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: A memorandum prepared by the Secretary of the Treasury explaining the bill in greater detail is also attached.
shared_material.explanation: Nearly parallel supporting-document language and administrative machinery strongly indicate reuse.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I will appreciate it if you will lay the draft legislation before the House of Representatives
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It would be appreciated if you would lay the proposed legislation before the House.
shared_material.explanation: The closing request is materially and verbally parallel.
